note: Track beat (theory-basics), step 4: sixteenths counted "1 e and a", then a rest on the number and a rest on the "and", against the click and over drums. Missing: a rhythm tool that shows a written rhythm with its rests and listens to the claps; backing-band's click sounds only the beat.

exercise.title: Sixteenths and rests
exercise.why: A sixteenth is a quarter of a beat, so counting "1 e and a" gives every clap a word, and a rest is a word you say without clapping.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. Count "1 e and a, 2 e and a" aloud, each number on a click, and clap on every word.
Practice until the four claps are even and the next number lands on the click.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Keep saying the whole count, and clap only on "e and a": the click sounds where your clap is missing.
If the claps drift, clap every word again for a bar.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Clap on each number, on "e" and on "a", and say "and" without a clap.
When the silent "and" takes as long as a clap, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If a stage is too fast, go back one and count aloud again.

Press Play below to start the drums. Clap a bar of sixteenths, then a bar with a rest on every number, and keep swapping.
Then press Click below to switch the metronome on, and check that the numbers of your count land on it.
